rationale: No supported optimization preserves the intended build and test coverage for this workflow. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (fail-fast: true on matrices) is contraindicated because every matrix outcome (compiler x standard x suite across Linux/macOS/Windows) is a distinct required portability result; canceling remaining cells on one failure would lose required diagnostics, and the supporting evidence is synthetic with negligible measured savings (485s -> 482s, no elapsed percent). P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is contraindicated because these are legitimate long C++ build/test jobs with existing 120-minute budgets; the evidence example used a 5-minute bound, and valid slow runs would exceed any tighter limit. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE offers only modest aggregate benefit (6% free / 3.4% paid) from analyst illustration, involves mutable/unchecked cached content (apt PPA packages, git clones), and is not a clear safe win. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is already implemented via the existing concurrency block with cancel-in-progress: true. Test/build selection patterns (P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT) would reduce coverage and are barred by their own contraindications (full test set required; required checks must run on each revision). P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT lacks representative timing data in the provided history. Therefore no change is supported.
